rationale: Built the deterministic prefix the mechanism hypothesis asked for and it reproduces the guard's gap directly: a leader whose log already holds a committed joint-entering change that it has not applied (pending_conf_index=0, applied=0, committed=2, joint_now=false) accepts a second joint-entering proposal and appends it as EntryConfChangeV2 at index 3 instead of rewriting it to a normal entry. That is the propose-time guard passing on exactly the pair of inputs the hypothesis named - alreadyPending false because pendingConfIndex does not cover the committed change, and alreadyJoint false because this leader never applied it - so the second joint-entering change reaches the log, and every node that applies the log in order meets the second change with a joint tracker, which is what the sweep's three rejections show. The prefix stands in for the leadership change that produces that leader-local state: the command Appends the change directly and then sets pendingConfIndex to the applied index, so what it demonstrates is the guard's response to a reachable state rather than the full history that reaches it. I request isolated execution so the operands are receipt-backed before the finding's mechanism is stated as observed; the asserted defect claim itself already rests on the sweep receipt and is unchanged.

scope.description: Adds a deterministic case (TestAssuranceStaleGuardPrefix) to the fixed harness: one voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) becomes leader, appends a JointImplicit learner-add ConfChangeV2 and has it committed without applying it, then has pendingConfIndex set to its applied index (the staleness a leadership change can leave behind) and proposes the same joint-entering change again through the real MsgProp path; one CA_EVENT reports pendingConfIndex, applied, committed, whether the tracker is joint, and the type and index of the resulting last log entry. Probes A-C, the sweep and the earlier deterministic joint-change case are unchanged.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, withPeers, confChangeToMsg, appendEntry, Step with MsgProp, allEntries); no production logic is modified.

The committed-but-unapplied state and the stale pendingConfIndex are supplied by the case rather than produced by an election sequence; the case therefore demonstrates the guard's response to that state, not the history that creates it.
The second proposal uses the same ConfChangeV2 as the first, so the observation is about the guard's decision, not about which change was requested.
Randomness is fixed per seed elsewhere; this case is deterministic.

experiment.prefix: r := newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); r.becomeCandidate(); r.becomeLeader(); cc := ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit, Changes: [{AddLearnerNode, 4}]}; msg, _ := confChangeToMsg(cc); r.appendEntry(msg.Entry); r.raftLog.commitTo(r.raftLog.lastIndex()); r.pendingConfIndex = r.raftLog.applied; then r.Step(&pb.Message{Type: MsgProp, From: 1, Entries: msg.Entry}) and emit CA_EVENT stale_guard_prefix with pendingConfIndex, applied, committed, joint_now and the last entry's type and index.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation with the deterministic guard prefix added (TestAssuranceStaleGuardPrefix) to observe the propose-time guard under leader-local state that a leadership change can leave: a committed joint-entering change this leader has not applied together with a pendingConfIndex that predates it. A draft-side run reported pending_conf_index=0, applied=0, committed=2, joint_now=false and second_proposal_entry_type=EntryConfChangeV2 at index 3, i.e. the guard appended the second joint-entering change, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
